finding.claim: The DELETE /reports/:id handler calls the async authorize() without await. The 403 is thrown inside a promise that nobody awaits, so execution continues straight to db.reports.remove() and any authenticated user can delete any report whatever their grants. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which can crash the process on modern Node.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (a session with a user) sends DELETE /reports/<id> for a report they have no 'delete' grant on. The id comes from req.params.id.

trace.note: The report is loaded by id with no ownership check
authorize(...) returns a Promise that is not awaited, so the forbidden error is never observed
The grants check runs asynchronously, and its throw at lines 11-14 only rejects the dropped promise
The report is removed and 204 returned regardless of the authorization result

finding.guards_checked: The authorize() function itself is correct, and the PUT handler at server.js:27 awaits it properly, so the flaw is specific to DELETE. There is no other middleware or route-level authorization. The only middleware (server.js:4-7) copies req.session.user and does no authorization. No error-handling middleware catches the rejection.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 on missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at line 20, so the check is ineffective. The middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user. There is no other authorization or error-handling middleware.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so its throw at server.js:14 only rejects a dropped promise and server.js:21 db.reports.remove() runs regardless of grants, which lets any session user delete any report. The unhandled rejection can also crash the process on modern Node.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at server.js:20, so the rejection is dropped. The only middleware (server.js:4-7) just copies the session user. There is no error-handling middleware.
verdict_facts.reason: server.js:20 calls authorize() as a bare, un-awaited statement, so its 403 throw (server.js:11-14) only rejects a dropped promise and server.js:21 db.reports.remove() runs for any authenticated user, unlike the PUT handler, which awaits it at server.js:27.
